objectives: Say the name of your favourite animal.
Say where an animal lives and what it eats.
Use the animal words and know what they mean.
Describe an animal step by step, from its body to its home.
Answer questions about your favourite animal.
Be kind and safe when you meet an animal.

sections.body:
Most children have a **favourite animal**. It might be a cat, a dog, a bird, a fish, a horse, or an elephant. It might be an animal at the zoo, or a small one living under your bed.

Animals are easy to talk about. You can say things you can see. *It has four legs. It has a long tail. It has soft brown fur.*

You can also say where it lives. *It lives in a house with us.* *It lives in the sea.* *It lives in the forest.*

And you can say what it eats. *It eats fish.* *It eats seeds.* *It eats grass.*

Three things — the body, the home, the food — are enough to describe almost any animal. Add the sound it makes and you have said everything there is to say.

Talking about animals is also easy to share. A friend who likes dogs will listen to you talk about dogs. That is how children make friends.

In this book you will learn how to describe an animal in order, how to answer questions about it, and how to be safe and kind when you meet one.
examples: My favourite animal is the elephant.
It has a long trunk and grey skin.
It lives in the forest and eats leaves.
sections.heading: Everyone has an animal they love most

sections.body:
The name of an animal is the first thing you say about it. Most animal names are easy to guess.

**A dog** says *woof*. **A cat** says *meow*. **A cow** says *moo*. **A duck** says *quack*. **A lion** says *roar*. **A bird** says *tweet*.

Some animals have sounds that are not words at all. A bee says *buzz*. A snake says *hiss*. A mouse squeaks.

Animals also have names for what they wear. **Fur** is the soft hair of a cat or a dog. **Feathers** cover a bird. **Scales** cover a fish. **A shell** covers a turtle. **A mane** is the long hair around a lion's neck. **Wings** let a bird fly.

You can use these words to make a sentence anybody understands. *My cat has soft fur and a long tail. She says meow when she is hungry.*

And the sound is often the funniest part. Say it out loud when you tell somebody. Your friend will know the animal straight away.
examples: A duck says quack, and my duck says it very loudly.
The elephant has thick grey skin and a long trunk.
My rabbit has soft fur and long ears.
sections.heading: Naming animals and the sounds they make

sections.body:
These are the words you need when you talk about animals.

**Pet** is an animal that lives with people. *My dog is a pet. He sleeps on my bed.*

**Wild animal** is an animal that lives on its own in nature. *A tiger is a wild animal. You should never go near one.*

**Farm animal** is an animal that people keep to help them. *Cows give us milk. Chickens give us eggs.*

**Habitat** is the place an animal lives. *The desert is the camel's habitat. A pond is the frog's habitat.*

**Endangered** means an animal is in danger of disappearing for ever. *The giant panda is endangered. There are not many left.*

**Extinct** means the animal is already gone. Nobody has seen one for hundreds of years. *The dinosaur is extinct.*

**Mammal** is an animal with fur and warm blood. *A whale is a mammal. So is a bat.*

**Bird** is an animal with feathers and wings. *A sparrow is a bird. So is a penguin.*
examples: A camel lives in the desert.
The dinosaur is extinct. We only know it from fossils.

sections.body:
Every animal has a **habitat**. That is the place where it lives and finds food.

Some animals live with people. A dog sleeps in a house. A cat lives in a house. A fish lives in a bowl of water. These are pets.

Some animals live on a farm. Cows, goats, pigs and chickens live there. People keep them because they give us milk, eggs and meat.

Some animals live in the wild. A lion lives in the grass of Africa. A tiger lives in a hot forest in Asia. A polar bear lives on cold ice. A monkey lives high in the trees.

Some animals live in the water. A fish lives in the sea. A dolphin swims in the ocean. A frog lives near a pond. A turtle can walk on land and swim in the sea.

And some animals live in the air. A bird lives in a nest. A bee lives in a hive. A bat hangs in a cave by day and flies at night.

You can say it like this: *An eagle lives in the sky. It has wings and it eats fish. It has a white head and a hooked beak.*

Ask about the habitat when you meet a new animal. It is the best way to learn something new.
examples: A bee lives in a hive and makes honey.
Whales and dolphins live in the ocean.
A hamster is a pet that lives in a cage.
sections.heading: Where animals live

sections.body:
Follow this order and your friend will see the animal in their head.

First, **name** it. *My favourite animal is the elephant.*

Next, **describe its body**. *It has a long trunk, big ears and thick grey skin.*

Then, **say where it lives**. *It lives in the forest in Africa.*

After that, **say what it eats**. *It eats leaves and fruit.*

Then, **say the sound it makes**. *It trumpets, and it is very loud.*

Last, **say one thing you love about it**. *I love that it helps the other animals in its herd.*

Now pause and let your friend ask a question. *How big is it?* *How long does it sleep?* *Can it swim?* Answer the ones you know, and say *I am not sure* about the others. It is much better to say that than to make something up.
examples: My favourite animal is the dolphin.
It has a smooth grey skin and a long nose.
I love that dolphins play together.
sections.heading: How to describe your favourite animal
steps: Say one thing you love about it.
Let your friend ask a question.

sections.body:
Animals can be lovely, and some of them can hurt you too. Here is how to stay safe and kind at the same time.

When you meet an animal you do not know, **stand still** and let it come to you. Do not run at it and do not grab it.

**Let the animal sniff you first.** A dog that smells your hand is being polite. Your hand is a hand, not a toy.

**Never pull an animal's tail or ears.** That hurts, and a hurt animal may bite.

**Wash your hands** after you touch an animal, and after you clean up animal mess. This is a rule for everybody, every time.

**Do not feed wild animals.** Bread makes birds and dolphins ill. Feeding one is not kind, even when it looks hungry. If an animal is hungry, its family is probably close by.

And if you see an animal that is hurt or alone, do not try to fix it yourself. Tell a grown-up. A grown-up can call the right people.

Being kind to animals means being gentle, being calm, and being far away when you should be.
examples: Let the dog smell my hand first.
I will wash my hands after I feed the rabbit.
The bird is hurt. We need to tell a grown-up.
sections.heading: Being kind and safe with animals

item.summary: Most children have an animal they love most. After reading this you can name your favourite animal, say where it lives and what it eats, and describe an animal so well that somebody else can picture it.
